gaps.explanation: Pass 7 re-read pp5, 9-13 (p14 is a statistical table). Nothing is missing and nothing is counted twice: every p5 fund column has exactly one source in detail (General p9, ARPA p10, Keno p11, Papillion Landing p12, Papio Bay p13 budget schedules; Debt Service and Capital Projects p5 columns, which have no schedule). Per fund, detail vs p5 Total revenues: General 59,058,061 (p9 Actual Total revenues; its 18 lines add to it) vs 29,588,079 = +29,469,982; ARPA 1,825,788 (p10) vs 14,230 = +1,811,558 (p10 prints Federal grants 1,811,558 that the p5 GAAP ARPA column does not show); Keno 719,702 (p11) vs 726,446 = -6,744; Papillion Landing 2,214,771 (p12) vs 2,209,727 = +5,044; Papio Bay 367,112 vs 367,112 = 0; Debt Service 4,445,749 = 4,445,749; Capital Projects 6,948,734 = 6,948,734. Sum +31,279,840 = the gap. Almost all of it is one printed figure: p9 (report p60) prints General Fund 'Taxes - city sales' Actual 31,635,831 (Final budget 12,106,917, Variance 19,528,914, Total revenues 59,058,061 and Excess 23,387,239 all consistent with it), while the p5 General column prints Taxes - city sales 2,297,264 (+29,338,567). The rest of General (+131,415) is budgetary vs GAAP row differences (e.g. p9 'Proceeds from auction' 110,898, which p5 shows as other financing 'Proceeds from sale of capital assets' 64,360). The figures are printed as they are; the report's budget schedule and statement do not agree. Nothing to add or remove.

Per fund, detail vs p5 Total expenditures: General 32,629,114 (p9 printed lines 31,980,393 + p5 General 'Recreation department' 640,346 + lease Principal payments 8,213 + Interest on leases 162; p9 prints Total expenditures 32,606,794 but no Recreation row) vs 32,746,737 = -117,623; Keno 271,258 (p11) vs 279,233 = -7,975; Papillion Landing 2,114,354 (p12 2,110,678 + p5 lease 3,659 + 17) vs 2,096,586 = +17,768; Papio Bay 355,877 (p13) vs 351,568 = +4,309; ARPA 0 = 0; Debt Service 11,001,216 and Capital Projects 9,191,838 tie. Net schedule short by 103,521 = the gap. These are the printed budgetary-basis actuals vs the GAAP columns; no printed row is missing and none is duplicated.
